The only durable primary store. Harbur creates/reuses one root folder and one appData document. Repository bytes are ZIP artifacts, not one Drive file per source file.
Global shell: schema, config, settings, manifests, watches, users,
storageVersion exists after load; missing app-data bootstraps.
Portable repository manifest beside the ZIP artifact. Repository creators
receive triage, merge, and settings maintainer permissions.
Compact per-repo index: file metadata, README/assets sidecars, repo ZIP id,

activity, repositoryStorageVersion after load. No persisted diff.
Per issue/PR detail after compaction: body, comments, reviews, edits.
Selected detail routes load only the selected thread document; unreadable
Hot append records for issue/PR create, comments, title/body edits, issue
state changes, PR reviews, PR closes. PR create appends contain only
base/proposal artifact identity and PR ZIP id; no diff or file payload.
Current repository code snapshot. Browser downloads via a temporary
Drive copy/link for PR creation, selected review hydration, preview,
or repository ZIP download. Server never extracts or streams
this archive body in any workflow.
Complete immutable PR proposal ZIP. Browser downloads a temporary Drive
copy/link for selected PR detail and proposal preview. Only changed-file
display data stays in the bounded browser diff cache.
Global app-data without backupCredentials, repo index/thread JSON,
repository ZIPs, manifests, PR ZIPs. ZIP artifacts are copied Drive-to-Drive
with temporary source permission; append records are materialized into
owners.json, public-repos.json, user-access/<email-hash>.json only if global
app-data read becomes measured bottleneck. Public indexes may be Vercel
Reason: compact JSON keeps shell reads small; ZIP artifacts avoid one Drive request per source
Reason: append files let independent thread mutations avoid overwriting the same repo index.
Reason: README/assets sidecars make overview renders skip large ZIP extraction.
Reason: full proposals stay in PR ZIPs; list routes keep artifact references only.

Write paths, parallel mutation model, and recovery
High-frequency thread mutations create separate append JSON files.
Later repository loads compact appends into per-thread docs
No queue, no lock service, no DB transaction. Parallel
users write separate UUID files into the repo folder.
GoogleDriveConflictError -> reload latest state -> retry repo
mutation up to 3 attempts. Drive adapter retries transient
Browser downloads the base ZIP, filters the proposed folder, computes the
local UX diff, and uploads a complete proposal ZIP directly to Drive.
Server accepts no diff/files and stores only immutable artifact identity.
Browser loads the proposal for safe local metadata hydration and sends only
repo identity + PR number. Server revalidates permission, strict base,
proposal checksum, and artifact-bound review, then asks Drive to copy
the exact proposal ZIP into the repository.
Move exact Drive-side proposal copy into repo folder; save affected PR thread
and repo index with expected version. Delete previous repo ZIP only
after metadata save succeeds and no snapshot references it.
Repository delete removes repo folder as one Drive object.
Due backups reload full state, fold appends into the mirror,
Reason: append write is close to the practical Drive-only floor: one Drive file create per successful thread mutation.
Reason: save order keeps old ZIP valid until metadata commit succeeds and cleans new artifacts on failure.

Base64url JSON ticket + HMAC-SHA256 signs actorEmail, kind,
uploadFolderId, zipBytes, origin, expiresAt, target, and for PR

Uploads repository, GitHub mirror, full PR proposal,
or mirror-sync ZIP bytes directly to a temporary Drive upload URL.
Merge uses an exact Drive-side copy. No Drive token, client secret,
or refresh token reaches the browser.

Commit repository/PR upload or promote PR proposal
Repo/GitHub create: validate metadata/sidecars, save manifest/index;
stage id becomes repo root. PR: validate Drive envelope/base ZIP id,
store full proposal id/checksum, never diff/files. Merge: strict base +
review/checksum, exact Drive copy. Mirror: validate metadata/base id.
Known failures/cancel delete staged upload folders immediately.
Expired upload-* stages are swept before later uploads after TTL+grace.
When enabled in admin settings, browser reads GitHub API tree data,
fetches raw/blob file bytes without .gitignore, uploads through a signed
staged Drive session, and refreshes only during admin sessions when due.
Normal public/user reads never fetch GitHub.
Client validates for immediate UX; server remains authoritative. README/assets sidecars are capped and verified by hash; repository exports exclude Harbur
metadata folders such as issues/, pulls/, activity/, feeds/, audit/, settings/, credentials/.
Reason: large upload bytes bypass serverless request-body limits; committed-download bytes come from temporary
Drive API media copies while server still owns authorization and final commit.
Reason: keeping sidecars in the index makes README overview fast without duplicating the repository ZIP.
OAuth client id, required restricted Drive API key, transient GIS code,
HttpOnly cookie, temporary upload URL, signed ticket, filtered AppState.
GOOGLE_DRIVE_CLIENT_SECRET, owner refresh token, auth-code exchange,
ID-token verification, role refresh from APP_ADMIN_EMAILS, access-token
Backup refresh tokens live only in primary owner appData
backupCredentials. Backup mirror never serializes backupCredentials back
Private repos and maps removed for unauthorized actors. Notifications
filtered by current visibility. backupCredentials stripped from all
Production cookie uses __Host-, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, no
Domain, Path=/. Google sign-in becomes Harbur session cookie.
Public visible to all. Private visible to admins, repository
maintainers, and explicit private grants. Names mutable; emails stable.
Every mutation is authenticated when required, role-checked,
Issue/PR policy controls create and merge. Reviewed merge requires
another merge-capable user; PR authors cannot review their own PR.
Reason: browser gets capabilities, not secrets; server is the only token exchange and Drive-authorizing boundary.
Reason: visibility is enforced after every load, so stale client hints cannot reveal private repo data.
Design decisions, tradeoffs, and measured follow-ups
Google Drive has higher latency than DB/object storage, versioned files instead of
transactions, API quota, and transient 429/5xx risk. Harbur keeps deployment simple:
Shell reads one small global doc. Repo operations read one repo index plus appends.
Route-scoped merge avoids full app-state reload. Server access-token memoization is
Metadata split by hotness: global shell, per-repo index, per-thread detail, append
records, repository ZIP, PR ZIP. No per-file Drive writes. No app-level serialization
Append records are UUID-idempotent materialization inputs; high-frequency
thread writes avoid repo-index rewrites until compaction. Mutable JSON uses
expectedVersion/retry for settings, watches, cleanup, merge, and backup status.
No Google secret leaves backend. Owner token is server env. Backup tokens stay in
primary appData. Returned AppState is filtered and credentials stripped.
The current design favors one global manifest plus per-repo indexes.
Extra public/user indexes would add repair and consistency paths.
Keep Google SSO + Harbur HttpOnly sessions, owner Drive credentials server-only, one immutable content ZIP per repo version plus
current index/thread JSON, optimistic versions/ETags, public reads as unauthenticated server functions that return public data only,
private/user indexes uncached, every mutation server-validated before Drive writes.
Close to Drive write floor: every successful thread mutation still needs at least one Drive file create.
Public reads use server functions and Drive state directly; no resident server cache.
Current indexes: global app-data manifest plus compact per-repository index/thread JSON.
ZIP upload and merge paths keep archive bytes out of server request bodies.
